findings.text: Deferred unthrottle entry executes in the context of a single run queue whose identity arrives as opaque argument. It establishes single clock refresh semantics for the whole drain by refreshing once and then suppressing further refreshes until the drain completes. During suppression it removes each element from the deferred collection and invokes release only for elements still flagged as throttled.

Unthrottle interface for a fair group queue refreshes current execution state before deciding eligibility. When bandwidth enforcement is active and remaining allowance is not positive the call leaves throttling intact and returns without side effects beyond accounting refresh. Otherwise it clears throttling and reconciles hierarchical and leaf membership before considering processor wakeup.

Clock loop suppression is guarded by run queue ownership. Activation asserts ownership and warns when suppression is already engaged, then engages it. Deactivation asserts ownership and disengages it. The flag exists to avoid repeated clock work while iterating over many queues.

Unthrottle path maintains the invariant that a queue with enforcement enabled and exhausted allowance stays throttled. Allowance is evaluated after catching up execution accounting, so asynchronous consumption between grant and arrival cannot cause an immediate rethrottle after release.

Throttle release transitions through detachment plus time accounting plus hierarchical propagation plus leaf repair plus wakeup evaluation. Detachment removes the queue from the throttled set. When a throttle start moment was recorded, elapsed time is added to cumulative throttled duration and the marker cleared. Propagation walks upward through ancestors, leaf repair reattaches empty weight queues that still carry decay work, and wakeup is requested only when the current occupant is idle and fair work is queued.

Teardown behavior varies by configuration. Fair bandwidth destruction can be an empty operation. Real time bandwidth destruction terminates the associated period timer. Real time group unregistration does nothing when group scheduling is disabled, otherwise destroys bandwidth only when a per group entity exists, while the alternate build provides an empty unregistration. Fair group unregistration in the shown interface is also empty.

Grace period completion for group removal recovers the group object from the embedded callback link and delegates to synchronous unregistration. The contract ensures that queue structures are not released until all readers from the earlier detachment have completed.

Processor group membership lifecycle separates creation plus activation plus deactivation plus release plus destruction. Creation yields the existing root for the top level and otherwise allocates a child, signaling exhaustion as out of memory. Activation brings extensible state online first and aborts the whole activation on failure, then links into the hierarchy when a parent exists and refreshes effective utilization bounds. Deactivation only retires extensible state, release detaches scheduling state, and destruction finalizes unregistration depending on the quiet interval since release.

Extensible online state uses presence and initialization markers. At entry already marked groups trigger a one time warning. Without cgroup integration the operation only marks presence. With integration it resolves either the hierarchy scheduler or the root scheduler for legacy groups, optionally calls group initialization with weight plus bandwidth period plus quota plus burst plus idle preference, normalizes errors, and on success stores the scheduler and marks both presence and initialization. The alternate header form reports success without touching state.

Extensible offline state requires prior presence and warns when absent. With integration active and initialization previously successful and an exit handler available, the handler runs for the departing group. The stored scheduler is then cleared and both markers removed. The alternate header form is empty.

Scheduler resolution for groups and knob writes demands holding either the global cgroup coordination lock or the extensible operations semaphore. Groups lacking an associated cgroup are treated as the root. Resolution yields a scheduler only when initialization previously succeeded, and knob handling for the top level resolves through the root while others resolve through the parent.

Migration validation plus commit plus cancellation form a three phase interface. Validation checks real time feasibility for each task when real time grouping is enabled and then consults extensible validation, with fallback forms accepting unconditionally. Commit relocates every task in the supplied set without per task failure handling. Cancellation invokes only extensible cleanup to withdraw provisional preparation.

Real time placement is rejected only when grouping is enabled and the candidate is a real time task and the destination allowance equals zero. This preserves the invariant that admitted real time tasks always have a feasible execution path. All other placements are accepted.

Extensible migration preparation maintains strict pairing between preparation and later handling. Moves where origin and destination coincide are ignored to match core behavior, as are moves that change the task home scheduler since those surface through task lifecycle events instead. Remaining moves optionally run a preparation handler and then record the origin on the task. Failure triggers optional cancellation for all previously recorded tasks and clears every mark, and explicit cancellation repeats that clearing pass.

Conversion carrier for utilization clamp input contains a scaled percentage field plus a capacity equivalent plus a status indicator. The carrier preserves user intent across parsing and application so that display can reproduce the original request rather than a rounded reconstruction.

Decimal percentage handling fixes precision at 2 fractional digits and full scale at 10000 units. Power of ten support builds decimal scale factors by pasting an exponent onto base ten notation through nested helpers. Bandwidth period configuration bounds the maximum at 1 second and the minimum at 1 millisecond, both expressed in microseconds.

Utilization clamp controls accept either the keyword max or a decimal percentage. Input is trimmed, the keyword selects full capacity, otherwise fixed point parsing with two digit precision runs and values above full scale are rejected as out of range with valid inputs converted to capacity by shifting and rounded scaling. Writes enable the clamp mechanism once and then under coordination update the requested value only on change while always storing exact percentage and refreshing effective bounds. Display prints max at full capacity and otherwise prints integer and fractional parts with fixed width, served through separate minimum and maximum file operations.

Clamp handling preserves exact user percentage separately from rounded capacity to survive irreversible rounding divergence between requested and stored forms. Effective bounds always track the tightest applicable bound after each write and after group activation.

Share and weight interfaces translate between user shares and internal load plus extensible weight. Write clamps excessive values to a defined ceiling, applies scaled load to the group, and mirrors the extensible weight only on success. Read returns scaled shares when fair grouping exists and otherwise derives weight from the extensible value through rounding with a factor of 1024 over the default. Extensible weight update serializes with the operations semaphore, resolves the knob scheduler, optionally notifies on change, and always stores the new value.

Bandwidth reconfiguration serializes with a dedicated constraints mutex plus system wide CPU read protection to coordinate with offline handling and runtime flag updates. Global schedulability validation runs before any mutation. Per bandwidth updates use interrupt safe spin protection, while per CPU queue updates each take the corresponding run queue interrupt safe lock.

Bandwidth reconfiguration converts microsecond inputs to nanoseconds with a distinguished infinite quota preserved as infinite. Usage tracking is enabled before related changes when transitioning from unlimited to limited and disabled after when transitioning back. Under protection the period plus quota plus burst are installed, runtime is refilled and clamped, and the period timer restarts when limited. Each online processor then gets enforcement enabled with primed remaining allowance and any still throttled queue is released. Quota toggling uses a static key in one build and empty operations in the alternate.

Schedulability validation walks the whole group tree under read protection after normalizing proposed values to microseconds when limited. Each group computes a normalized ratio with unlimited represented as infinite, the root is always infinite, and hierarchical quota is the constrained minimum along the ancestry. Default hierarchy inherits parent quota when the child is unlimited and otherwise takes the smaller of child and parent, while legacy hierarchy only inherits when unlimited and rejects a limited child exceeding a limited parent.

Schedulability check carrier holds a target group reference plus a period value plus a quota value. It distinguishes the group under proposal from ancestors whose current settings are read back during the walk.

Runtime refill is a no operation for infinite quota. Otherwise it adds a full quota to accumulated runtime, treats any excess over the previous snapshot as burst consumption by accumulating time and count, and then clamps total runtime to quota plus burst while updating the snapshot. This preserves the invariant that stored runtime never exceeds one quota plus allowed burst.

Bandwidth statistics files expose cumulative counters with fixed labels. The main file reports nr_periods plus nr_throttled plus throttled_time plus nr_bursts plus burst_time, and additionally reports wait_sum aggregated across all possible processors only when statistics are enabled and the group is not the root. The local file reports only throttled_time summed across possible processors as self attributed duration using single load semantics per processor.

Read side and spin discipline spans unthrottle plus group lifecycle plus clamp handling plus validation plus weight updates. Deferred unthrottle combines run queue locking with read protection to stabilize group lifetime across list traversal. Bandwidth detachment uses non interrupt spin scope while reconfiguration uses interrupt safe scope. Clamp writes and online activation combine mutex plus read protection, validation holds read protection across the tree walk, and extensible weight updates hold the operations read semaphore.

Several races require explicit handling. Deferred list iteration can trigger clock work and group freeing, mitigated by single clock refresh with suppression plus queue locking plus read annotation. Asynchronous runtime consumption can leave negative remaining allowance at unthrottle entry, handled by refresh plus recheck. Final group destruction depends on the quiet interval between release and free, and extensible preparation failures require unwinding already prepared tasks to preserve pairing.
